title: Gradual Weighted Failover Guidance and Telemetry Checklist
body:
Purpose:
This note collects a pragmatic, operator-friendly checklist and example telemetry thresholds for performing a gradual weighted failover between regions (aka progressive traffic shift) when a region shows systemic degradation but is still partially reachable. The goal is to minimize user impact, preserve request affinity where possible, and keep rollback paths fast and well-instrumented.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to region-to-region traffic shifts for the Redwood inference control plane and data plane paths (API gateways + inference endpoints).
- Assumes warm standby in secondary region(s): capacity pre-provisioned, models deployed and warmed, KV caches optionally preseeded.
- Assumes ability to adjust routing weights via traffic-control-plane (weighted-LB) and to change DNS TTLs via Route53/CloudDNS.
- Primary failure modes addressed: regional control-plane latency amplification, egress saturation, regional network congestion, partial edge loss. Not intended for total region blackout (use emergency cold cutover playbook).

Pre-flight checks (run these before any weight changes):
1) Capacity and readiness
   - Confirm warm-standby nodes in target region report RUNNING and >90% of required model replicas present.
   - Confirm autoscaler in target region can accept burst (check reserved GPUs free >= anticipated peak QPS).
   - Command examples: 
     - infra CLI: infra status region-us-west-2 --models=all --min-ready=1
     - kubectl ctx us-west-2 get pods -l app=inference -o wide
2) Model and artifact sync
   - Verify model versions match (git tag or model-id). If quantized variants are used, validate compatibility matrix.
3) KV cache and prefix seeding
   - If using kvcache preseed, confirm top N prefixes have been seeded to target region and TTLs are active.
   - Check kvcache hit rate baseline.
4) Control plane health
   - Ensure control-plane metrics (deployment controller, autoscaling loop latencies) are healthy in target region.
5) Observability and rollback tooling
   - Confirm dashboards and alerts for latency, 5xx rate, queue depth, CPU/GPU util, and egress saturations are visible for both regions.
   - Prepare quick rollback links and scripts (traffic-weight-set --region X --weight Y).
6) Communications
   - Post to #sre-alerts and #eng-status with planned window. Notify on-call and product leadership.

Telemetry baselines and trigger thresholds (recommendations):
- Latency P95 increase: trigger cautious shift if source region P95 > baseline * 1.4 for 5m.
- Error rate: if 5xx-rate > 1.5x baseline and sustained for 3m, elevate to aggressive shift.
- Queue depth/backpressure: if request queue length > 3x baseline or backlog increases for 2 consecutive 1m buckets, prepare shift.
- Egress saturation: if NIC egress >= 85% for 5m, consider shifting read-heavy traffic.
- KVcache miss surge: sharp drop in kvcache hit rate (>20% drop) implies cache warming benefits target region.

Stepwise weighted shift (recommended conservative sequence):
- Phase 0 (Validation): weights unchanged, set DNS TTL to 30s (if currently higher) to allow faster propagation for next phases. Monitor for 5m.
- Phase 1 (Micro-canary): shift 1% weight to target region for 2m. Verify request success, latency, and token throughput.
- Phase 2 (Slow ramp): 5% -> 10% -> 20% with 3–5m holds. At each hold verify: 5xx rate, P95, GPU util.
- Phase 3 (Moderate ramp): 30% -> 50% with 5–10m holds. If any metric degrades beyond rollback thresholds, revert to last safe weight.
- Phase 4 (Stabilize): 75% -> 90% with 10m holds. If stable for 15m at 90%, either complete cutover or continue gradual to 100%.
- Phase 5 (Complete): set weight 100% and restore DNS TTL to normal (300s typical).

Rollback criteria (stop and rollback immediately to previous safe weight if any of the following):
- Absolute 5xx rate > 2% of requests for sustained 3m window (unless baseline higher).
- P95 latency spike > 2x baseline for sustained 3m.
- Critical SLO alerts firing (eg inference-failure-high).
- Downstream services (billing, auth) show cascading errors attributable to shift (investigate before continuing).

Example control commands (operational snippets):
- Adjust routing weight via controller: 
  curl -X POST \"$TRAFFIC_CTRL/api/v1/weights\" -d '{\"from\":\"us-east-1\",\"to\":\"us-west-2\",\"weight\":10}' 
- Query weight: infra routing get-weights --from us-east-1
- Temporary DNS TTL change (Route53): aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://change.json --hosted-zone-id Z12345 (change.json with TTL 30)
- kvcache preseed: kvcache seed --region us-west-2 --prefix-file top20-prefixes.txt

Observability checklist during shift (runbook steps):
- Watch these dashboards live: api/latency-by-region, kvcache/hit-miss-by-region, gpu/utilization, egress/throughput.
- Open the following logs for tails: gateway-access.log (filter target region), inference-worker.log (ERROR only).
- Keep a running table in incident Slack thread with time, weight change, P95, 5xx%, GPU util.

Edge cases and operational notes:
- Mixed affinity requests: some customers pin models to specific region endpoints. For those, coordinate with solutions engineering to migrate or add endpoint aliases rather than global weight shifts.
- Long-tail sessions: streaming or long requests may keep connections open; ensure connection draining windows are honored when reducing weight—prefer soft drain (stop new requests, let existing finish) over hard kill.
- DNS caching by client ISPs: even with low TTLs, some clients cache longer — plan for a gradual tail and keep origin stable until tails drain.
- KV cache cold start costs: be mindful that heavy preseed will increase initial egress and compute; stagger seeding if bandwidth constrained.

Post-shift actions and RCA inputs to collect:
- Collect timeline with exact weight deltas and associated metric snapshots.
- Attach perf traces for 10 requests per phase (sampled) showing request path and latencies.
- Gather a list of anomalous 5xx errors with stack traces and correlation IDs.
- Note actions taken (DNS TTL changes, kvcache seeding commands) and time to completion.
- Save metric extracts to S3: s3://redwood-sre/incident-exports/<incident-id>/

Playbook decision matrix (quick reference):
- If only control-plane is impacted (controllers slow but worker healthy) => increase routing weight cautiously but keep an eye on deployment latencies.
- If data-plane latencies spike and GPU util high => prefer routing to region with lower GPU saturation even if DNS changes needed.
- If region shows persistent network flakiness (packet loss >2%) => favor DNS-based redirection and reduce cross-region dependencies.

Communication template (Slack/incident):
- Short status update: [Time UTC] Starting weighted shift: us-east-1 -> us-west-2, starting 1% -> target 100% over ~2h if stable. Reason: region us-east-1 edge degradation. On-call: @oncall-sre. Links: dashboard, routing UI, kvcache status.
- Escalation: if rollback triggered, post rollback reason and retained weight.

Open questions and follow-ups (for postmortem):
- Can we automate safe rollbacks based on composite alerts to remove manual checks?
- Should we add a pre-flight probe that simulates a 50qps synthesis load to validate metrics before ramp?
- Validate if TTL 30s is safe for our largest customers without violating CDN contract TTL minimums.

Appendix: quick checklist (one-liner):
- [ ] Confirm warm standby health
- [ ] Seed kvcache top prefixes
- [ ] Lower DNS TTL to 30s
- [ ] Start 1% micro-canary
- [ ] Ramp by holds and validate at each step
- [ ] Restore TTL and document timeline

Notes: This doc is an operational draft—please add runbook automation snippets and commands you used during the next incident into the linked GitHub PR for infra/routing so we can build a safe-automation pipeline.

Owners for follow-up: Diego (automation), Rina (telemetry tuning), Omar (kvcache strategy).
